clue.text: Thugs apparently let out rob men at random

indicators.note: random signals letters taken in no set order, so the three words are shuffled together

explanation.surface: Hooligans released from custody go about robbing men indiscriminately.
explanation.walkthrough: 'random' rearranges the letters of 'rob men at'. The definition plays on a hired crowd of thugs being one that is, apparently, let out for rent.
explanation.definitionFit: A hired crowd of troublemakers is a mob that is rented, that is let out for payment.

clue.text: Tough, pioneering therapy finally used on one's back

indicators.note: used on says the following pieces are placed on, that is after, the first piece
back here asks for the little word for one's to be read in the opposite direction

parts.note: one's is a contraction of one is, giving I and IS read as I'S
pioneering work is new, original work

indicators.note: finally picks the final letter of the word therapy

explanation.surface: A tough new treatment is finally applied to someone's back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' gives SI; 'used on' puts the rest after it. 'pioneering' looks like it describes the therapy, but it stands alone as a synonym.
explanation.definitionFit: Sinewy means wiry and muscular, so physically tough and strong.

clue.text: What's said by clergy to get men in a muddle

indicators.note: in puts the piece for men inside the clergy's service

parts.note: a priest says mass, the eucharistic service
OR is other ranks, ordinary soldiers or men as against officers

explanation.surface: Priests' words leave the congregation confused.
explanation.walkthrough: OR, the military abbreviation for other ranks, goes inside MASS.
explanation.definitionFit: A morass is figuratively a confusing, entangling mess, literally a bog.

clue.text: Swede, game, volunteers appropriate answer

parts.note: RU is rugby union, a game
TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's volunteer reserve force
to bag something is to appropriate or take it

explanation.surface: A Scandinavian, a match and some volunteers make a fitting reply.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Swede' looks like a nationality, but it is the root vegetable, called a rutabaga in North America.
explanation.definitionFit: Rutabaga is the North American name for the yellow root vegetable the British call swede.

clue.text: Smart word of welcome also to send to hosts

indicators.note: hosts means the first piece holds the second inside it, as a host has a guest

parts.note: cc on an email or letter lists others to send copies to
hi is an informal greeting

explanation.surface: A stylish greeting also goes to everyone hosting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'also to send to' describes the copy line on an email or memo; 'hosts' makes it hold the greeting.
explanation.definitionFit: Chic means stylish and elegant, the sense of smart as in well dressed.

clue.text: Heavy vehicle runs over a stranger, amusingly

parts.note: R is the cricket scoring abbreviation for runs
O is the cricket abbreviation for an over
taken as written
droller means more comically odd, stranger in an amusing way

explanation.surface: A heavy lorry runs down an unknown person, which someone finds funny.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stranger' looks like a person run over, but it is the comparative adjective, with 'amusingly' giving DROLLER.
explanation.definitionFit: A road roller is the heavy machine used to flatten road surfaces.

clue.text: Have got to go on about favourite city

indicators.note: to go on says this piece goes on, after, the others

parts.note: CA is circa, about
a pet is a favourite, as in teacher's pet
to own is to have got something

explanation.surface: Someone insists on carrying on about their best-loved town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to go on' places the possession word after the rest, as 'on' can mean following. 'favourite city' reads as one phrase, but 'city' alone defines.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the South African city at the foot of Table Mountain.

clue.text: Establishments after time would become capital

indicators.note: after time would become capital says these letters plus T in front make the capital, so take T away

parts.note: Tunis is the capital of Tunisia

explanation.surface: Institutions would turn into the centre of things given time.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue says UNIS would become TUNIS after T, so the answer is that capital minus T. 'would become' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Unis is informal for universities, which are educational establishments.

clue.text: Ill will after abandonment by church and state

indicators.note: after abandonment by says the church's letters have left the word

parts.note: malice is ill will, a wish to harm
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: Bad feeling lingers after both church and state are deserted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'church and state' looks like one phrase; 'church' is CE taken from MALICE, and 'state' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Mali is a landlocked country, a state, in West Africa.

clue.text: Scoring century having broken duck

indicators.note: having broken says the century letter splits open the word for zero

parts.note: a duck in cricket is a score of nothing
C is the Roman numeral for a hundred, a century

explanation.surface: A batsman scores a hundred after getting off the mark from nought.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a duck is a score of zero, and a century is a hundred runs; C goes inside NOTHING.
explanation.definitionFit: Notching means scoring, as in notching up points or runs.

clue.text: Pole rude to chum and policeman is sorry

parts.note: N is the north pole

indicators.note: rude here means crude or rough, so the letters are roughly rearranged

parts.note: a cop is a policeman

explanation.surface: A Polish man is rude to his friend and a police officer apologises.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rude' rearranges TOCHUM into OTMUCH. 'Pole' looks like a nationality, but it gives N.
explanation.definitionFit: Sorry here means poor or inadequate, as in a sorry effort; British slang for not very good.

clue.text: Informal refusal after putting Frank's name forward

indicators.note: putting with forward says one letter is moved to the front
forward is where the letter for name is put, at the start of the word

parts.note: frank means open and candid

explanation.surface: Someone flatly says no after putting Frank's name forward.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Frank' looks like a man's name; it is the adjective, OPEN, whose N moves to the front.
explanation.definitionFit: Nope is a casual, colloquial way of saying no.

clue.text: Seafood on reflection stuff caught in Channel port mostly

indicators.note: this word is a container marker: it says one piece is placed inside the other, and the clue words of the pieces show which way round
mostly says the port loses its last letter

parts.note: Calais is the French port on the English Channel

indicators.note: on reflection asks for the word for stuff to be read as a mirror image, backwards

parts.note: to ram is to stuff or cram

explanation.surface: Thinking it over, a fish dish got stuck at a Channel crossing point.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' trims the port to CALAI; 'on reflection' gives MAR, and 'caught in' puts that inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Calamari is squid served as food, a seafood dish.

clue.text: Spirit of minor player turned cooler

parts.note: a cog is a small part in a big machine, a minor player

indicators.note: turned asks for the slang word for prison to be read in reverse

parts.note: cooler and can are both slang for prison

explanation.surface: A bit-part actor's drink turned colder.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cooler' looks like colder, but it is slang for prison, CAN, which 'turned' makes NAC.
explanation.definitionFit: Cognac is a brandy, a type of distilled spirit from western France.

clue.text: State capital last up for redistribution

indicators.note: redistribution shares the letters out afresh, rearranging them

explanation.surface: The final item is offered again.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for redistribution' rearranges LASTUP.
explanation.definitionFit: Saint Paul is the capital city of Minnesota, a US state.

clue.text: Round article in case is wind instrument: that'll put price up

indicators.note: round says the instrument's letters go around the other pieces

parts.note: sax is short for saxophone, a wind instrument
lest means in case, for fear that
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A packed item turns out to be a saxophone, a costly addition.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Round' puts the instrument around the other pieces. The definition is a whole phrase describing what a levy on purchases does.
explanation.definitionFit: A tax levied on goods at the point of sale raises the price paid.

clue.text: Get by after upsetting and hard time

indicators.note: upsetting in a down clue turns the word over, reading it bottom to top

parts.note: to cope is to get by, manage
H is the pencil-grading abbreviation for hard

explanation.surface: Managing after an upset makes for a difficult period.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after upsetting' gives EPOC, reading the coping word upwards as this is a down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: An epoch is a period of time, an era.

clue.text: It's the March winds that kept Britain dry in the 80s!

definitions.text: that kept Britain dry in the 80s

indicators.note: winds is read as a verb, twisting the letters around

explanation.surface: Blustery spring weather once kept Britain dry, a joke about rain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'winds' rearranges ITSTHEMARCH. In 1980s British politics a dry was a hardline supporter of Margaret Thatcher's economic policy.
explanation.definitionFit: The policy creed of 1980s British Prime Minister Margaret Thatcher; her supporters were called dries.

clue.text: Rocket features compartment

parts.note: mush is slang for the face, its features
a room is a compartment of a building

explanation.surface: A space rocket includes a compartment.
explanation.walkthrough: MUSH is British slang for face. 'Rocket' looks like a noun but is the verb: to grow rapidly.
explanation.definitionFit: To mushroom is to grow or increase suddenly, just as prices may rocket.

clue.text: Negotiating assets to exclude winning damages?

parts.note: to bar is to exclude
gaining means winning, getting
chips means damages slightly, as a cup is chipped

explanation.surface: Bargaining counters may rule out compensation for winning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'damages' looks like a legal payout but is the verb, CHIPS.
explanation.definitionFit: Things held to trade away in negotiation are called bargaining chips.

clue.text: Like to get up and go round the world

indicators.note: get up in a down clue lifts the letters, reading them upwards

parts.note: as means like
to turn is to go round, rotate

explanation.surface: Someone wants to get up and travel round the globe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to get up' turns AS into SA.
explanation.definitionFit: Saturn is a planet, another world in the solar system.

clue.text: Run in marathon Aberdeen's holding

indicators.note: holding says the letters sit within the words marathon Aberdeen's

explanation.surface: A Scottish city stages a long-distance race.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Run' looks like the marathon, but 'Run in' is the definition, to arrest.
explanation.definitionFit: To run in someone is British slang for arresting them, as is to nab.

clue.text: Turning around new song in French beyond wit of composer

indicators.note: beyond in a down clue puts these letters after, below, the first piece

parts.note: a wag is a wit, a joker

indicators.note: turning around reverses the whole run of new, song and in French together

parts.note: an air is a song or tune
en is French for in

explanation.surface: A new French song is turned round by a humorous composer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turning around' gives NERIAN from the three pieces together; 'beyond' places it after the joker. 'of composer' is an adjectival definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Wagnerian means relating to the composer Richard Wagner or his music.

clue.text: What prevents pain in jaw cracking up?

parts.note: cracking up means laughing hard
jaw and gas both mean idle chatter

explanation.surface: What stops the pain of a jaw breaking?
explanation.walkthrough: 'jaw' and 'cracking up' look like an injury, but they are chatter and laughter. 'in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Nitrous oxide is used as an anaesthetic by dentists to dull pain.

clue.text: Fierce female with stake cut down slave colony founder?

parts.note: an Amazon was one of a legendary race of fierce female warriors

indicators.note: cut down says the stake word is trimmed of its last letter

parts.note: an ante is a stake in poker

explanation.surface: A ferocious woman with a pointed post kills a founder of a slave colony.
explanation.walkthrough: Amazon ant queens invade other ants' nests and use their workers as slaves.
explanation.definitionFit: Amazon ants raid other species' nests and found colonies worked by enslaved ants.

clue.text: Unusual play teeming with characters in Act I

indicators.note: teeming with characters says the letters of the two words swarm together into a new order

explanation.surface: An odd drama is crowded with people in its first act.
explanation.walkthrough: 'teeming with characters in' rearranges PLAY and ACTI together.
explanation.definitionFit: Atypical means not typical, unusual.

clue.text: Rough hand putting son over edge

indicators.note: over in a down clue places the son letter above the edge word

parts.note: to edge is to crawl, move slowly

explanation.surface: A rough labourer pushes his son off a cliff.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rough hand' looks like a worker, but 'hand' is handwriting; 'edge' is a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: A scrawl is messy handwriting, a rough hand.

clue.text: Square loaf mostly gobbled by old man

indicators.note: gobbled by puts the loaf word inside the father's letters

parts.note: pa is father, the old man

indicators.note: mostly removes the last letter

parts.note: to loaf is to laze

explanation.surface: Dad wolfs down most of a plain loaf of bread.
explanation.walkthrough: 'loaf' looks like bread but is the verb, LAZE, trimmed to LAZ.
explanation.definitionFit: A plaza is an open public square in a town.

clue.text: Oddly missing Latvian girl

indicators.note: oddly missing drops the letters in odd positions, keeping the even ones

explanation.surface: A Latvian girl has strangely disappeared.
explanation.definitionFit: Ava is a girl's first name.
